223	        # Final usage-only chunk (litellm emits this when include_usage is set).
224	        chunk3 = mock.MagicMock()
225	        chunk3.id = "chunk-3"
226	        chunk3.object = "chat.completion.chunk"

398	            call.args[i] == v for i, v in enumerate(args)

974	def _event_stream_message(headers: dict[str, str], payload: bytes) -> bytes:
975	    # AWS event stream framing: a prelude (total length, headers length, prelude CRC),
976	    # string-valued headers, the payload, then a CRC over the whole message.
977	    encoded_headers = b"".join(
978	        bytes([len(name)])
979	        + name.encode()
980	        + b"\x07"
981	        + struct.pack(">H", len(value))
982	        + value.encode()
983	        for name, value in headers.items()
984	    )
985	    prelude = struct.pack(">II", 16 + len(encoded_headers) + len(payload), len(encoded_headers))
986	    message = prelude + struct.pack(">I", zlib.crc32(prelude)) + encoded_headers + payload
987	    return message + struct.pack(">I", zlib.crc32(message))
988

990	def _bedrock_chunk(event: dict[str, Any]) -> bytes:
991	    return _event_stream_message(
992	        {":event-type": "chunk", ":content-type": "application/json", ":message-type": "event"},
993	        json.dumps({"bytes": base64.b64encode(json.dumps(event).encode()).decode()}).encode(),
994	    )

2	title: Model Providers
3	description: Supported LLM providers in MLflow AI Gateway including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, and Vertex AI. Configure endpoints and use passthrough APIs.
4	---
5	
6	import Tabs from "@theme/Tabs";
7	import TabItem from "@theme/TabItem";
8	
9	# Model Providers
10	
11	MLflow AI Gateway supports many model providers natively, without requiring any additional dependencies. For providers not listed here, you can optionally install [LiteLLM](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/providers) to extend the gateway to use them. LiteLLM is not a dependency of MLflow AI Gateway—it is only used if you choose to install it in your environment. This page covers the major providers, their capabilities, and how to use their passthrough APIs.
12	
13	## Supported Providers
14	
15	The AI Gateway supports providers across these categories:
16	
17	### Major Cloud Providers
18	
19	| Provider          | Chat | Embeddings | Passthrough API                                    |
20	| ----------------- | ---- | ---------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
21	| **OpenAI**        | Yes  | Yes        | `/gateway/openai/v1/...`                           |
22	| **Anthropic**     | Yes  | No         | `/gateway/anthropic/v1/...`                        |
23	| **Google Gemini** | Yes  | Yes        | `/gateway/gemini/v1beta/...`                       |
24	| **Azure OpenAI**  | Yes  | Yes        | Via OpenAI passthrough                             |
25	| **AWS Bedrock**   | Yes  | Yes        | Anthropic passthrough (Claude, API key auth)       |
26	| **Vertex AI**     | Yes  | Yes        | Anthropic, Gemini, or OpenAI passthrough, by model |
27	
28	### Additional Providers
29	
30	| Provider         | Chat | Embeddings | Notes                                |
31	| ---------------- | ---- | ---------- | ------------------------------------ |
32	| **Cohere**       | Yes  | Yes        | Command and Embed models             |
33	| **Mistral**      | Yes  | Yes        | Mistral AI models                    |
34	| **Groq**         | Yes  | No         | Open-source models                   |
35	| **Together AI**  | Yes  | Yes        | Open-source models                   |
36	| **Fireworks AI** | Yes  | Yes        | Open-source models                   |
37	| **Ollama**       | Yes  | Yes        | Local models                         |
38	| **Databricks**   | Yes  | Yes        | Foundation Model APIs                |
39	| **Portkey**      | Yes  | Yes        | Unified gateway for any LLM provider |
40	
41	For a complete list of supported providers, view the provider dropdown when creating an endpoint or see the [LiteLLM documentation](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/providers).
42	
43	### Evaluation Providers
44	
45	| Provider     | Model family | Passthrough API                  |
46	| ------------ | ------------ | -------------------------------- |
47	| **TypeSafe** | Jev          | `/gateway/typesafe/v1/systemone` |
48	
49	TypeSafe endpoints support structured System One evaluation requests. They do not support the gateway's chat, embeddings, OpenAI-compatible, or streaming APIs.
50	
51	## Provider-Specific Passthrough APIs
52	
53	### OpenAI
54	
55	The OpenAI passthrough exposes the full OpenAI API:
56	
57	**Base URL:** `http://localhost:5000/gateway/openai/v1`
58	
59	**Supported Endpoints:**
60	
61	- `POST /chat/completions` - Chat completions
62	- `POST /embeddings` - Text embeddings
63	- `POST /responses` - Responses API (multi-turn conversations)
64	
65	<Tabs>
66	<TabItem value="python" label="Python SDK" default>
67	
68	```python
69	from openai import OpenAI
70	
71	client = OpenAI(
72	    base_url="http://localhost:5000/gateway/openai/v1",
73	    api_key="dummy",  # Not needed, configured server-side
74	)
75	
76	# Chat completion
77	response = client.chat.completions.create(
78	    model="my-endpoint",
79	    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}],
80	)
81	
82	# Embeddings
83	embeddings = client.embeddings.create(
84	    model="my-embeddings-endpoint",
85	    input="Text to embed",
86	)
87	
88	# Responses API
89	response = client.responses.create(
90	    model="my-endpoint",
91	    input="Hello!",
92	)
93	```
94

96	<TabItem value="curl" label="cURL">
97	
98	```bash
99	# Chat completion
100	curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/gateway/openai/v1/chat/completions \
101	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
102	  -d '{"model": "my-endpoint", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]}'
103	
104	# Embeddings
105	curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/gateway/openai/v1/embeddings \
106	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
107	  -d '{"model": "my-embeddings-endpoint", "input": "Text to embed"}'
108	
109	# Responses API

115	</TabItem>
116	</Tabs>
117	
118	See [OpenAI API Reference](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference) for complete documentation.
119	
120	### Anthropic
121	
122	Access Claude models through the Anthropic passthrough:
123	
124	**Base URL:** `http://localhost:5000/gateway/anthropic`
125	
126	**Supported Endpoints:**
127	
128	- `POST /v1/messages` - Messages API
129	
130	<Tabs>
131	<TabItem value="python" label="Python SDK" default>
132	
133	```python
134	import anthropic
135	
136	client = anthropic.Anthropic(
137	    base_url="http://localhost:5000/gateway/anthropic",
138	    api_key="dummy",  # Not needed, configured server-side
139	)
140	
141	response = client.messages.create(
142	    model="my-endpoint",
143	    max_tokens=1024,
144	    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}],
145	)
146	print(response.content[0].text)
147	```
148	
149	</TabItem>
150	<TabItem value="curl" label="cURL">
151	
152	```bash
153	curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/gateway/anthropic/v1/messages \
154	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
155	  -d '{
156	    "model": "my-endpoint",
157	    "max_tokens": 1024,
158	    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]
159	  }'
160	```
161	
162	</TabItem>
163	</Tabs>
164	
165	See [Anthropic API Reference](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/api) for complete documentation.
166	
167	### Google Gemini
168	
169	Access Gemini models through Google's API format:
170	
171	**Base URL:** `http://localhost:5000/gateway/gemini`
172	
173	**Supported Endpoints:**
174	
175	- `POST /v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent` - Content generation
176	- `POST /v1beta/models/{model}:streamGenerateContent` - Streaming generation
177	
178	<Tabs>
179	<TabItem value="python" label="Python SDK" default>
180	
181	```python
182	from google import genai
183	
184	client = genai.Client(
185	    api_key="dummy",
186	    http_options={
187	        "base_url": "http://localhost:5000/gateway/gemini",
188	    },
189	)
190	
191	response = client.models.generate_content(
192	    model="my-endpoint",
193	    contents={"text": "Hello!"},
194	)
195	client.close()
196	print(response.candidates[0].content.parts[0].text)

203	curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/gateway/gemini/v1beta/models/my-endpoint:generateContent \
204	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \

208	</TabItem>
209	</Tabs>
210	
211	See [Google Gemini API Reference](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs) for complete documentation.
212	
213	### Vertex AI
214	
215	Vertex AI endpoints use the passthrough API of the model family they serve: Claude models take the [Anthropic](#anthropic) routes, Gemini models take the [Google Gemini](#google-gemini) routes, and partner MaaS models (Llama, Mistral, DeepSeek, and others) take the [OpenAI](#openai) routes. Requests are authenticated server-side with the endpoint's Google Cloud credentials.
216	
217	Vertex AI validates the `anthropic-beta` header against the betas it supports, which lag behind the Anthropic API, and rejects the whole request when it sees a value it does not know. The `vertex_anthropic_betas` option on a Claude endpoint controls which client-supplied beta values are forwarded:
218	
219	- Unset (default): the header is forwarded unchanged.
220	- An empty list: the header is dropped.
221	- A list of values, for example `["web-search-2025-03-05"]`: only those values are kept, and the header is dropped if none remain.
222	
223	The option is part of the model's Vertex AI configuration, alongside `vertex_project` and `vertex_location`. Through the API, `auth_config` values are strings, so pass the betas as a comma-separated string such as `"web-search-2025-03-05,interleaved-thinking-2025-05-14"`; an empty string drops the header.
224	
225	### Azure OpenAI
226	
227	Azure OpenAI uses the same passthrough as OpenAI with additional configuration:
228	
229	**Base URL:** `http://localhost:5000/gateway/openai/v1`
230	
231	When creating an Azure OpenAI endpoint:
232	
233	1. Select **Azure OpenAI** as the provider
234	2. Enter your Azure endpoint URL
235	3. Enter your Azure API key
236	4. Specify your deployment name
237	
238	```python
239	from openai import OpenAI
240	
241	client = OpenAI(
242	    base_url="http://localhost:5000/gateway/openai/v1",
243	    api_key="dummy",
244	)
245	
246	response = client.chat.completions.create(
247	    model="my-azure-endpoint",
248	    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}],
249	)
250	```

252	### Databricks Foundation Models
253	
254	Databricks Foundation Models APIs are OpenAI-compatible:
255	
256	**Base URL:** `http://localhost:5000/gateway/openai/v1`
257	
258	When creating a Databricks endpoint:
259	
260	1. Select **Databricks** as the provider
261	2. Enter your Databricks workspace URL
262	3. Enter your Databricks personal access token
263	4. Specify the model endpoint name
264	
265	```python
266	from openai import OpenAI
267	
268	client = OpenAI(
269	    base_url="http://localhost:5000/gateway/openai/v1",
270	    api_key="dummy",
271	)
272	
273	response = client.chat.completions.create(
274	    model="my-databricks-endpoint",
275	    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}],
276	)
277	```
278	
279	### TypeSafe
280	
281	The TypeSafe passthrough exposes TypeSafe's System One API through the MLflow Gateway. The gateway endpoint name goes in the request body's `model` field; the gateway forwards the request to the configured TypeSafe model with its server-side TypeSafe API key.
282	
283	**Base URL:** `http://localhost:5000/gateway/typesafe/v1`
284	
285	**Supported Endpoints:**
286	
287	- `POST /systemone` - System One structured evaluation
288	
289	```bash
290	curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/gateway/typesafe/v1/systemone \
291	  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
292	  -d '{
293	    "model": "jev-evaluator",
294	    "state": {
295	      "inputs": {"question": "How do I reset my password?"},
296	      "outputs": "Select Forgot password on the sign-in page."
297	    },
298	    "questions": {
299	      "evaluation": {
300	        "type": "noul",
301	        "instructions": "Does state.outputs answer the question in state.inputs?"
302	      }
303	    }
304	  }'
305	```
306	
307	TypeSafe gateway endpoints are raw System One endpoints, not chat endpoints. Use them for direct System One requests through Gateway-managed credentials. They are separate from MLflow judges that use `make_judge(model="typesafe:/...")`; do not pass a TypeSafe gateway endpoint as `model="gateway:/..."` to `make_judge()`.
308	
309	### Portkey
310	
311	[Portkey](https://portkey.ai) provides a single OpenAI-compatible API.
312	
313	In addition to your Portkey API key, Portkey needs to know which upstream provider
314	to route each request to. Configure one of the following when creating the endpoint:
315	
316	- **Provider Slug**: a [Model Catalog](https://portkey.ai/docs/product/model-catalog)
317	  integration slug prefixed with `@` (e.g. `@openai-prod`), or a bare provider slug
318	  (e.g. `openai`) together with a **Provider API Key** for that provider
319	- **Config ID or JSON**: a saved Portkey config ID (e.g. `pc-xxxx`) or a raw JSON config. This is stored as a secret, since a raw JSON config may embed upstream credentials
320	- Neither, if your model name already embeds the routing target
321	  (e.g. `@openai-prod/gpt-4o`) or your Portkey API key has a default config attached
322	
323	When creating a Portkey endpoint:
324	
325	1. Select **Portkey** as the provider
326	2. Enter your Portkey API key and a routing target as described above
327	3. Enter your Portkey base URL (e.g. `https://api.portkey.ai/v1`)
328	4. Enter the model name as per your Portkey configuration
329	   (e.g. `gpt-4o`, `@openai-prod/gpt-4o`, or a custom alias)
330	
331	```python
332	from openai import OpenAI
333	
334	client = OpenAI(
335	    base_url="http://localhost:5000/gateway/openai/v1",
336	    api_key="dummy",  # Not needed, configured server-side
337	)
338	
339	response = client.chat.completions.create(
340	    model="my-portkey-endpoint",
341	    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}],
342	)
343	print(response.choices[0].message.content)
344	```
345	
346	See [Portkey documentation](https://portkey.ai/docs) for the full list of supported models and configuration options.
347	
348	## Model Capabilities
349	
350	When creating endpoints, the model selector shows capability badges:
351	
352	| Badge         | Description                                  |
353	| ------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
354	| **Tools**     | Model supports function/tool calling         |
355	| **Reasoning** | Model has enhanced reasoning capabilities    |
356	| **Caching**   | Model supports prompt caching for efficiency |
357	| **Vision**    | Model can process images                     |
358	
359	Additional information displayed:
360	
361	- **Context window**: Maximum tokens the model can process
362	- **Token costs**: Input and output pricing per million tokens

1 --- 2 title: Query Endpoints 3 description: Query MLflow AI Gateway endpoints using the MLflow unified API, OpenAI-compatible chat completions interface, or native passthrough APIs for OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google Gemini. 4 --- 5 6 import Tabs from "@theme/Tabs"; 7 import TabItem from "@theme/TabItem"; 8 9 # Query Endpoints 10 11 Once you've created an endpoint, you can call it through several different API styles depending on your needs. 12 13 ## Supported API Styles 14 15 The following table summarizes the available gateway APIs: 16 17 | Category | API Style | URL Pattern | Description | 18 | --------------- | ---------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | 19 | **Unified** | MLflow Invocations | `POST /gateway/{endpoint_name}/mlflow/invocations` | Native MLflow interface supporting chat completions and embeddings. Handles routing features like traffic splitting and fallbacks. | 20 | **Unified** | OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions | `POST /gateway/mlflow/v1/chat/completions` | Drop-in replacement for the OpenAI chat completions API. Use the endpoint name as the `model` parameter. | 21 | **Unified** | OpenAI-compatible Models | `GET /gateway/mlflow/v1/models` | List configured gateway endpoint names in the OpenAI models format. | 22 | **Passthrough** | OpenAI | `POST /gateway/openai/v1/chat/completions`
`POST /gateway/openai/v1/embeddings`
`POST /gateway/openai/v1/responses` | Full OpenAI API access including Chat Completions, Embeddings, and Responses endpoints. | 23 | **Passthrough** | Anthropic | `POST /gateway/anthropic/v1/messages` | Direct access to Anthropic's Messages API. | 24 | **Passthrough** | Google Gemini | `POST /gateway/gemini/v1beta/models/{endpoint_name}:generateContent` | Google Gemini's native generateContent API. | 25 | **Passthrough** | TypeSafe | `POST /gateway/typesafe/v1/systemone` | Raw TypeSafe System One structured evaluation requests. | 26 27 ## Viewing Usage Examples 28 29 To see code examples for your endpoint, navigate to the Endpoints list and click either the Use button or the endpoint name itself. This opens a modal with comprehensive usage examples tailored to your specific endpoint. 30 31 ![Usage Modal](/images/genai/governance/ai-gateway/usage-modal.png) 32 33 The usage modal organizes examples into two categories: unified APIs that work across any provider, and passthrough APIs that expose provider-specific features. Within each category, the **Try it** tab lets you send a test request directly from the UI. 34 35 ## Unified APIs 36 37 Unified APIs provide a consistent interface regardless of the underlying model provider. These APIs make it easy to switch between different models or providers without changing your application code. 38 39 ### MLflow Invocations API 40 41 The MLflow Invocations API is the native interface for calling gateway endpoints. This API seamlessly handles model switching and advanced routing features like traffic splitting and fallbacks: 42 43 44 45 46 ```bash 47 curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/gateway/my-endpoint/mlflow/invocations \ 48 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 49 -d '{ 50 "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}], 51 "temperature": 0.7 52 }' 53 ``` 54 55 56 57 58 ```python 59 import requests 60 61 response = requests.post( 62 "http://localhost:5000/gateway/my-endpoint/mlflow/invocations", 63 json={"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}], "temperature": 0.7}, 64 ) 65 print(response.json()) 66 ``` 67 68 69 70 71 #### API Specification 72 73 The MLflow Invocations API supports both OpenAI-style chat completions and embeddings endpoints. 74 75 **Endpoint URL Pattern:** 76 77 ``` 78 POST /gateway/{endpoint_name}/mlflow/invocations 79 ``` 80 81 **Chat Completions Request Body:** 82 83 The request body follows the OpenAI chat completions format with these supported parameters. See [OpenAI Chat Completions API Reference](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/chat) for complete documentation. 84 85 | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | 86 | ------------------- | ------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | 87 | `messages` | array | Yes | Array of message objects with `role` and `content` fields | 88 | `temperature` | number | No | Sampling temperature between 0 and 2. Higher values make output more random. | 89 | `max_tokens` | integer | No | Maximum number of tokens to generate. | 90 | `top_p` | number | No | Nucleus sampling parameter between 0 and 1. Alternative to temperature. | 91 | `n` | integer | No | Number of completions to generate. Default is 1. | 92 | `stream` | boolean | No | Whether to stream responses. | 93 | `stream_options` | object | No | Options for streaming responses. | 94 | `stop` | array | No | List of sequences where the API will stop generating tokens. | 95 | `presence_penalty` | number | No | Penalizes new tokens based on presence in text so far. Range: -2.0 to 2.0. | 96 | `frequency_penalty` | number | No | Penalizes new tokens based on frequency in text so far. Range: -2.0 to 2.0. | 97 | `tools` | array | No | List of tools the model can call. Each tool includes `type`, `function` with `name`, `description`, and `parameters`. | 98 | `response_format` | object | No | Format for the model output. Can specify "text", "json_object", or "json_schema" with schema definition. | 99 100 **Response Format:** 101 102 ```json 103 { 104 "id": "chatcmpl-123", 105 "object": "chat.completion", 106 "created": 1677652288, 107 "model": "gpt-5", 108 "choices": [{ 109 "index": 0, 110 "message": { 111 "role": "assistant", 112 "content": "Hello! How can I assist you today?" 113 }, 114 "finish_reason": "stop" 115 }], 116 "usage": { 117 "prompt_tokens": 9, 118 "completion_tokens": 12, 119 "total_tokens": 21 120 } 121 } 122 ``` 123 124 **Streaming Responses:** 125 126 When `stream: true` is set, the response is sent as Server-Sent Events (SSE): 127 128 ``` 129 data: {"id":"chatcmpl-123","object":"chat.completion.chunk","created":1677652288,"model":"gpt-5","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":"Hello"},"finish_reason":null}]} 130 131 data: {"id":"chatcmpl-123","object":"chat.completion.chunk","created":1677652288,"model":"gpt-5","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":"!"},"finish_reason":null}]} 132 133 data: [DONE] 134 ``` 135 136 **Embeddings Request Body:** 137 138 For embeddings endpoints, the request body follows the OpenAI embeddings format. See [OpenAI Embeddings API Reference](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/embeddings) for complete documentation. 139 140 | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | 141 | ----------------- | --------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | 142 | `input` | string or array | Yes | Input text(s) to embed. Can be a single string or array of strings. | 143 | `encoding_format` | string | No | Format to return embeddings. Options: "float" (default) or "base64". | 144 145 **Embeddings Response Format:** 146 147 ```json 148 { 149 "object": "list", 150 "data": [{ 151 "object": "embedding", 152 "embedding": [0.0023064255, -0.009327292, ...], 153 "index": 0 154 }], 155 "model": "text-embedding-ada-002", 156 "usage": { 157 "prompt_tokens": 8, 158 "total_tokens": 8 159 } 160 } 161 ``` 162 163 ### OpenAI-Compatible Chat Completions API 164 165 For teams already using the OpenAI chat completion style APIs, the gateway provides an OpenAI-compatible interface. Simply point your OpenAI client to the gateway's base URL and use your endpoint name as the model parameter. This lets you leverage existing OpenAI-based code while gaining the gateway's routing capabilities. 166 167 See [OpenAI Chat Completions API Reference](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/chat) for complete documentation. 168 169 170 171 172 ```bash 173 curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/gateway/mlflow/v1/chat/completions \ 174 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 175 -d '{ 176 "model": "my-endpoint", 177 "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}], 178 "temperature": 0.7 179 }' 180 ``` 181 182 183 184 185 ```python 186 from openai import OpenAI 187 188 client = OpenAI( 189 base_url="http://localhost:5000/gateway/mlflow/v1", 190 api_key="", # API key not needed, configured server-side 191 ) 192 193 response = client.chat.completions.create( 194 model="my-endpoint", 195 messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}], 196 temperature=0.7, 197 ) 198 print(response.choices[0].message.content) 199 ``` 200 201 202 203 204 ### OpenAI-Compatible Models API 205 206 Use `GET /gateway/mlflow/v1/models` to discover named gateway endpoints in the active workspace. The response follows the OpenAI models list format. Each model's `id` is a gateway endpoint name that you can pass as the `model` parameter when querying the endpoint. 207 208 When MLflow authentication is enabled, users must authenticate and can list only endpoints they have `USE` permission on. Administrators can list all named endpoints in the active workspace. 209 210 The following examples assume the server does not require authentication: 211 212 213 214 215 ```bash 216 curl http://localhost:5000/gateway/mlflow/v1/models 217 ``` 218 219 220 221 222 ```python 223 from openai import OpenAI 224 225 client = OpenAI( 226 base_url="http://localhost:5000/gateway/mlflow/v1", 227 api_key="not-required", 228 ) 229 230 for model in client.models.list(): 231 print(model.id) 232 ``` 233 234 235 236 237 ## Passthrough APIs 238 239 The Passthrough API relays requests to the provider's LLM endpoint using its native formats, allowing you to use their native client SDKs with the MLflow Gateway. While unified APIs work for most use cases, passthrough APIs give you full access to provider-specific features that may not be available through the unified interface. 240 241 For detailed information on passthrough APIs for each provider, see [Model Providers](/genai/governance/ai-gateway/endpoints/model-providers). 242 243 ### TypeSafe Passthrough 244 245 TypeSafe passthrough endpoints accept raw System One requests at `POST /gateway/typesafe/v1/systemone`. These endpoints are for structured evaluation with TypeSafe's native request schema. They do not support chat completions, embeddings, mixed TypeSafe/chat routing, or streaming. 246 247 ```bash 248 curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/gateway/typesafe/v1/systemone \ 249 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 250 -d '{ 251 "model": "jev-evaluator", 252 "state": {"answer": "Select Forgot password on the sign-in page."}, 253 "questions": { 254 "helpful": { 255 "type": "noul", 256 "instructions": "Does state.answer help the user reset a password?" 257 } 258 } 259 }' 260 ``` 261 262 The `model` value is the MLflow Gateway endpoint name. For MLflow judges, use direct TypeSafe model URIs such as `model="typesafe:/jev-latest"`; TypeSafe gateway endpoints are not `gateway:/` judge models for `make_judge()`. 263 264 ### OpenAI Passthrough 265 266 The OpenAI passthrough API exposes the full OpenAI API including Chat Completions, Embeddings, and Responses endpoints. See [OpenAI API Reference](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference) for complete documentation. 267 268 269 270 271 ```bash 272 # Chat Completions API 273 curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/gateway/openai/v1/chat/completions \ 274 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 275 -d '{ 276 "model": "my-endpoint", 277 "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}] 278 }' 279 280 # Responses API 281 curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/gateway/openai/v1/responses \ 282 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 283 -d '{ 284 "model": "my-endpoint", 285 "input": "Hello!" 286 }' 287 ``` 288 289 290 291 292 ```python 293 from openai import OpenAI 294 295 client = OpenAI( 296 base_url="http://localhost:5000/gateway/openai/v1", 297 api_key="dummy", # API key not needed, configured server-side 298 ) 299 300 # Chat Completions API 301 response = client.chat.completions.create( 302 model="my-endpoint", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}] 303 ) 304 print(response.choices[0].message.content) 305 306 # Responses API 307 response = client.responses.create( 308 model="my-endpoint", 309 input="Hello!", 310 ) 311 print(response.output_text) 312 ``` 313 314 315 316 317 ### Anthropic Passthrough 318 319 Access Anthropic's Messages API directly through the gateway. See [Anthropic API Reference](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/api) for complete documentation. 320 321 322 323 324 ```bash 325 curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/gateway/anthropic/v1/messages \ 326 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 327 -d '{ 328 "model": "my-endpoint", 329 "max_tokens": 1024, 330 "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}] 331 }' 332 ``` 333 334 335 336 337 ```python 338 import anthropic 339 340 client = anthropic.Anthropic( 341 base_url="http://localhost:5000/gateway/anthropic", 342 api_key="dummy", # API key not needed, configured server-side 343 ) 344 345 response = client.messages.create( 346 model="my-endpoint", 347 max_tokens=1024, 348 messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}], 349 ) 350 print(response.content[0].text) 351 ``` 352 353 354 355 356 ### Google Gemini Passthrough 357 358 The Gemini passthrough API follows Google's API structure. See [Google Gemini API Reference](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs) for complete documentation. 359 360 361 362 363 ```bash 364 curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/gateway/gemini/v1beta/models/my-endpoint:generateContent \ 365 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 366 -d '{ 367 "contents": [{ 368 "parts": [{"text": "Hello!"}] 369 }] 370 }' 371 ``` 372 373 374 375 376 ```python 377 from google import genai 378 379 client = genai.Client( 380 api_key="dummy", 381 http_options={ 382 "base_url": "http://localhost:5000/gateway/gemini", 383 }, 384 ) 385 386 response = client.models.generate_content( 387 model="my-endpoint", 388 contents={"text": "Hello!"}, 389 ) 390 client.close() 391 print(response.candidates[0].content.parts[0].text) 392 ``` 393 394 395 396 397 ## Framework Integrations 398 399 The MLflow AI Gateway's OpenAI-compatible API makes it easy to integrate with popular LLM frameworks. Simply point your framework to the gateway's base URL and use your endpoint name as the model. 400 401 402 403 404 ```python 405 from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI 406 407 llm = ChatOpenAI( 408 model="my-endpoint", 409 base_url="http://localhost:5000/gateway/mlflow/v1", 410 api_key="not-needed", 411 ) 412 response = llm.invoke("Hello!") 413 print(response.content) 414 ``` 415 416 417 418 419 ```python 420 from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI 421 from langgraph.prebuilt import create_react_agent 422 423 llm = ChatOpenAI( 424 model="my-endpoint", 425 base_url="http://localhost:5000/gateway/mlflow/v1", 426 api_key="not-needed", 427 ) 428 graph = create_react_agent(llm, tools=[]) 429 result = graph.invoke({"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]}) 430 print(result["messages"][-1].content) 431 ``` 432 433 434 435 436 ```python 437 import dspy 438 439 lm = dspy.LM( 440 model="openai/my-endpoint", 441 api_base="http://localhost:5000/gateway/mlflow/v1", 442 api_key="not-needed", 443 ) 444 dspy.configure(lm=lm) 445 program = dspy.Predict("question -> answer") 446 print(program(question="What is MLflow?").answer) 447 ``` 448 449 450 451 452 ```python 453 import openai 454 from agents import Agent, Runner, set_default_openai_client 455 456 client = openai.AsyncOpenAI( 457 base_url="http://localhost:5000/gateway/openai/v1", 458 api_key="not-needed", 459 ) 460 set_default_openai_client(client) 461 462 agent = Agent(name="Assistant", instructions="You are helpful.", model="my-endpoint") 463 result = await Runner.run(agent, input="Hello!") 464 print(result.final_output) 465 ``` 466 467 468 469 470 ```python 471 import litellm 472 473 response = litellm.completion( 474 model="openai/my-endpoint", 475 messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}], 476 api_base="http://localhost:5000/gateway/mlflow/v1", 477 api_key="not-needed", 478 ) 479 print(response.choices[0].message.content) 480 ``` 481 482 483 484 485 ## Using Gateway Endpoints with Workspaces 486 487 When [workspaces](/self-hosting/workspaces/getting-started) are enabled on your MLflow server, you can specify the target workspace for a request by including the `X-MLFLOW-WORKSPACE` header. 488 489 :::note 490 The `X-MLFLOW-WORKSPACE` header is only relevant when the MLflow server is running with workspaces enabled (`--enable-workspaces` flag). If a default workspace is configured (often `default`) and you omit this header, the request will be served from that default workspace. The header is strictly required when you want to target a non-default workspace, or when no default workspace is configured. 491 ::: 492 493 494 495 496 ```bash 497 # Query endpoint in a specific workspace 498 curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/gateway/my-endpoint/mlflow/invocations \ 499 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 500 -H "X-MLFLOW-WORKSPACE: team-a" \ 501 -d '{ 502 "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}], 503 "temperature": 0.7 504 }' 505 ``` 506 507 508 509 510 ```python 511 import requests 512 513 # Query endpoint in a specific workspace by including the header 514 response = requests.post( 515 "http://localhost:5000/gateway/my-endpoint/mlflow/invocations", 516 json={"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}], "temperature": 0.7}, 517 headers={"X-MLFLOW-WORKSPACE": "team-a"}, 518 ) 519 print(response.json()) 520 ``` 521 522 523 524 525 ```python 526 from openai import OpenAI 527 528 # Create OpenAI client with workspace header 529 # External SDKs like OpenAI must explicitly set the header via default_headers 530 client = OpenAI( 531 base_url="http://localhost:5000/gateway/mlflow/v1", 532 api_key="", 533 default_headers={"X-MLFLOW-WORKSPACE": "team-a"}, 534 ) 535 536 response = client.chat.completions.create( 537 model="my-endpoint", 538 messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}], 539 ) 540 print(response.choices[0].message.content) 541 ``` 542 543 544 545 546 The workspace header applies to all gateway API endpoints, including: 547 548 - MLflow Invocations API (`/gateway/{endpoint_name}/mlflow/invocations`) 549 - OpenAI-compatible API (`/gateway/mlflow/v1/*`) 550 - Passthrough APIs (`/gateway/openai/v1/*`, `/gateway/anthropic/v1/*`, `/gateway/gemini/v1beta/models/{endpoint_name}:*`, `/gateway/typesafe/v1/systemone`) 551 552 For more details on workspace configuration and management, see the [Workspaces documentation](/self-hosting/workspaces/getting-started). 553 554 ## Using Gateway Endpoints with MLflow Judges 555 556 AI Gateway endpoints can be used as the backing LLM for MLflow's [LLM Judges](/genai/eval-monitor/scorers/#llms-as-judges). This allows you to run judge evaluations through the gateway, benefiting from centralized API key management and cost tracking. 557 558 To use a gateway endpoint as a judge model, use the `gateway:/` prefix followed by your endpoint name: 559 560 561 562 563 ```python 564 from mlflow.genai.scorers import Correctness 565 566 # Use a gateway endpoint for the Correctness judge 567 scorer = Correctness(model="gateway:/my-chat-endpoint") 568 ``` 569 570 571 572 573 ```python 574 from mlflow.genai.judges import make_judge 575 from typing import Literal 576 577 # Create a custom judge using a gateway endpoint 578 coherence_judge = make_judge( 579 name="coherence", 580 instructions=( 581 "Evaluate if the response is coherent and maintains a clear flow.\n" 582 "Question: {{ inputs }}\n" 583 "Response: {{ outputs }}\n" 584 ), 585 feedback_value_type=Literal["coherent", "somewhat coherent", "incoherent"], 586 model="gateway:/my-chat-endpoint", 587 ) 588 ``` 589 590 591 592 593 For more details on creating and using LLM judges, see the [LLM Judges documentation](/genai/eval-monitor/scorers/#llms-as-judges). 594

35	def _to_anthropic_content_parts(content: list[Any]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
36	    """Translate OpenAI-format multimodal content parts to Anthropic's shape.
37	
38	    ``image_url`` base64 data URLs become Anthropic ``image`` blocks with a base64
39	    ``source``; text parts pass through. Non-base64 image URLs are left as a text note
40	    since the judge image tool only ever emits base64 data URLs.
41	    """
42	    parts: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
43	    for part in content:
44	        if part.get("type") == "image_url":
45	            url = part.get("image_url", {}).get("url", "")
46	            if parsed := parse_base64_data_url(url):
47	                mime, data = parsed
48	                parts.append({
49	                    "type": "image",
50	                    "source": {"type": "base64", "media_type": mime, "data": data},
51	                })
52	            else:
53	                parts.append({"type": "text", "text": f"[unsupported image reference: {url}]"})
54	        else:
55	            parts.append(part)
56	    return parts

59	def _normalize_anthropic_input_tokens(
60	    token_usage: dict[str, int] | None,
61	) -> dict[str, int] | None:
62	    """Anthropic's input_tokens excludes cache tokens. Add them so input_tokens
63	    represents the total input (consistent with OpenAI/Gemini).
64	    """
65	    if not token_usage or TokenUsageKey.INPUT_TOKENS not in token_usage:
66	        return token_usage
67	    cache_read = token_usage.get(TokenUsageKey.CACHE_READ_INPUT_TOKENS, 0)
68	    cache_creation = token_usage.get(TokenUsageKey.CACHE_CREATION_INPUT_TOKENS, 0)
69	    if cache_read or cache_creation:
70	        token_usage[TokenUsageKey.INPUT_TOKENS] += cache_read + cache_creation
71	        if TokenUsageKey.TOTAL_TOKENS in token_usage:
72	            token_usage[TokenUsageKey.TOTAL_TOKENS] += cache_read + cache_creation
73	    return token_usage

100	def _extract_anthropic_streaming_token_usage(chunk: bytes) -> dict[str, int]:
101	    """
102	    Extract token usage from an Anthropic Messages streaming chunk.
103	
104	    Anthropic streaming format:
105	    - message_start event: {"message": {"usage": {"input_tokens": X, ...}}}
106	    - message_delta event: {"usage": {"output_tokens": Y}}
107	
108	    Returns:
109	        A dictionary with token usage found in this chunk.
110	        Total is calculated by the base class after accumulation.
111	    """
112	    usage: dict[str, int] = {}
113	    for data in parse_sse_lines(chunk):
114	        match data:
115	            case {
116	                "type": "message_start",
117	                "message": {"usage": dict(msg_usage)},
118	            }:
119	                if (input_tokens := msg_usage.get("input_tokens")) is not None:
120	                    usage[TokenUsageKey.INPUT_TOKENS] = input_tokens
121	                if (cached := msg_usage.get("cache_read_input_tokens")) is not None:
122	                    usage[TokenUsageKey.CACHE_READ_INPUT_TOKENS] = cached
123	                if (created := msg_usage.get("cache_creation_input_tokens")) is not None:
124	                    usage[TokenUsageKey.CACHE_CREATION_INPUT_TOKENS] = created
125	            case {"type": "message_delta", "usage": {"output_tokens": int(output_tokens)}}:
126	                usage[TokenUsageKey.OUTPUT_TOKENS] = output_tokens
127	    # Anthropic's input_tokens excludes cache tokens; normalize to include them.
128	    return _normalize_anthropic_input_tokens(usage) or usage

135	def _enforce_strict_schema(schema: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
136	    """Recursively set ``additionalProperties: false`` on object types that have ``properties``.
137	
138	    Anthropic's structured outputs require every object node to explicitly set
139	    ``additionalProperties: false``. Pydantic-generated schemas often violate
140	    this — for example, ``dict[str, str]`` produces:
141	
142	        // Rejected by Anthropic (400)
143	        {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": {"type": "string"}}
144	
145	    This function rewrites it to:
146	
147	        // Accepted by Anthropic
148	        {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": false}
149	
150	    Objects without ``properties`` (i.e. free-form dicts like ``dict[str, str]``)
151	    are left unchanged so the model can still populate them with arbitrary keys.
152	    """
153	    if not isinstance(schema, dict):
154	        return
155	    if schema.get("type") == "object":
156	        if "properties" not in schema:
157	            raise _UnsupportedSchemaError(
158	                "Object type without 'properties' (free-form dict) cannot be represented "
159	                "with Anthropic structured outputs, which require additionalProperties: false."
160	            )
161	        schema["additionalProperties"] = False
162	    for value in schema.values():
163	        match value:
164	            case dict():
165	                _enforce_strict_schema(value)
166	            case list():
167	                for item in value:
168	                    if isinstance(item, dict):
169	                        _enforce_strict_schema(item)

689	        tool_call_indices: dict[int, int] = {}

692	        async for chunk in stream:
693	            chunk = chunk.strip()

707	            if resp["type"] == "message_start":
708	                metadata["id"] = resp["message"]["id"]
709	                metadata["model"] = resp["message"]["model"]
710	                # Capture input_tokens and cache tokens from message_start

715	                    if (created := message_usage.get("cache_creation_input_tokens")) is not None:
716	                        usage_data["cache_creation_input_tokens"] = created

def test_claude_adapter_applies_vertex_fields_without_provider_hooks():
    """Formatting through ``adapter_class`` alone must produce a Vertex-valid payload.

    ``_prepare_payload`` is a provider hook reached only from ``AnthropicProvider._chat``
    and ``._chat_stream``. Callers that build a request from the adapter and post it
    themselves -- the judge path in ``mlflow.genai.judges.adapters.gateway_adapter``
    does exactly this -- never run that hook, so Vertex rejected the request with
    "anthropic_version: Field required". The transformation therefore has to live on the
    adapter, as it already does for Bedrock.
    """
    from mlflow.gateway.providers.vertex_ai import _VERTEX_ANTHROPIC_VERSION

def _disable_if_gateway_disabled(func):
    @wraps(func)
    def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
        if not MLFLOW_ENABLE_AI_GATEWAY.get():
            raise MlflowException(GATEWAY_DISABLED_MESSAGE, NOT_IMPLEMENTED)
        return func(*args, **kwargs)

    return wrapper

def catch_mlflow_exception(func):
    @wraps(func)
    def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
        try:
            return func(*args, **kwargs)
        except MlflowException as e:
            response = Response(mimetype="application/json")
            response.set_data(e.serialize_as_json())
            response.status_code = e.get_http_status_code()
            if response.status_code >= 500:
                is_debug = _logger.isEnabledFor(logging.DEBUG)
                msg = f"Error in {func.__name__}: {e}"
                if not is_debug:
                    msg += ". Set MLFLOW_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG for traceback."
                _logger.error(msg, exc_info=is_debug)
            return response

    return wrapper

def _validate_gateway_secret_auth_config(
    auth_config: dict[str, Any] | None,
) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    """Validate a gateway secret's ``auth_config`` on write and return a normalized copy.

    ``api_base`` is the only key naming an outbound target. A blank value is dropped rather
    than stored, since providers fall back to their default by truthiness.
    """
    if not auth_config:
        return None
    normalized = dict(auth_config)
    if reserved := sorted(_GATEWAY_AUTH_CONFIG_RESERVED_KEYS & set(normalized)):
        raise MlflowException.invalid_parameter_value(
            f"auth_config must not contain {', '.join(map(repr, reserved))}: these LiteLLM "
            "options choose where the gateway sends requests. Set the upstream with "
            "'api_base', which is validated."
        )
    api_base = normalized.get("api_base")
    if isinstance(api_base, str):
        api_base = api_base.strip()
    if not api_base:
        normalized.pop("api_base", None)
        return normalized
    _validate_gateway_api_base(api_base)
    normalized["api_base"] = api_base
    return normalized
